Question: Describe your low-code/no-code workflow designer for defining agentic workflows: conditional logic, loops, parallel processing.
Response: Two builder experiences. (1) Pro-code (primary): GHCP SDK in Python — skills define capabilities declaratively in SKILL.md markdown files. Durable Functions orchestrations define workflow graphs with conditional logic, loops, parallel fan-out/fan-in, and HITL gates in Python code. This is the recommended path for autonomous multi-step agent workflows. (2) Low-code: Copilot Studio provides a visual workflow designer with drag-and-drop canvas, conditional branching, loops, and parallel processing. Copilot Studio agents are supported via Agent 365 and natively integrated into the Custom Control Plane UI. We do not recommend Copilot Studio for complex autonomous agent workflows (it is optimised for conversational agents), but it is available for simpler citizen-developer use cases and for building agent surfaces in Teams/Copilot. (3) Configuration-driven: the Custom Control Plane UI provides a low-code configuration surface for operational parameters — skill library management, tool catalog, governance rules, autonomy dials, template fork-and-customise. No code required for operational configuration.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK (Python), Azure Durable Functions, Copilot Studio, Custom Control Plane UI
POC Demo: POC1: Show workflow definition in Durable Functions with parallel invoice processing and HITL gates. Show Control Plane configuration of autonomy thresholds.

Question: How are agent performance and process status monitored? Describe re-run and terminate capabilities.
Response: Monitoring operates at three levels. (1) Fleet Manager agent: continuously reasons about fleet health, SLA risk, and anomalies from OTEL telemetry. Composes the exception-only view for the Control Plane — operators see only workflows needing attention. (2) Foundry Control Plane: platform-level monitoring with agent run rates, error rates, token usage, cost, and execution traces. Foundry Evaluators run continuous quality checks. (3) Custom Control Plane UI: operator dashboard with real-time workflow status, filterable by agency, market, risk level, jurisdiction, client, workflow type. Re-run: Durable Functions supports replaying a workflow from a specific checkpoint — useful when an external system was down and the phase needs to retry. Terminate: operators can terminate a workflow from the Control Plane, which cancels the Durable Functions orchestration and triggers compensating actions for any revocable steps already executed.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager agent, Foundry Control Plane, Custom Control Plane UI, Durable Functions replay/cancel
POC Demo: POC1: Show workflow terminate from Control Plane with compensating actions. Show re-run of a failed phase from checkpoint.

Question: Describe automatic retry, human notification, graceful fallback, and escalation mechanisms for error handling.
Response: Exception handling is layered. (1) Agentic loop level: GHCP SDK sessions handle transient errors within the loop — the model reasons about failures and can retry tool calls with adjusted parameters. (2) Durable Functions level: configurable retry policies with exponential backoff per phase. After max retries, the phase enters exception state. (3) Fleet Manager level: the Fleet Manager detects exceptions and composes contextual notifications — what happened, what was tried, what it recommends, what the options are. Notifications route to the appropriate human via their PA and preferred surface (Teams, email Adaptive Card, Control Plane). (4) Escalation: if the assigned human does not act within an SLA window, Durable Functions timer triggers escalation to the next level (configured per workflow). (5) Graceful fallback: if a primary integration is unavailable (e.g. Workday API down), the agentic loop can fall back to cached data or queue the phase for later retry. If a model endpoint is unavailable, APIM AI Gateway fails over to an alternative model.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK error handling, Durable Functions retry/timer, Fleet Manager exception routing, APIM model failover
POC Demo: POC1: Simulate API timeout on Maconomy — show retry with backoff, fallback, and Fleet Manager notification to Finance BP.

Question: Describe the dashboard for human oversight: role-based views, customisation, visual agent activity monitoring.
Response: The Custom Control Plane UI is a purpose-built React application providing fleet-scale human oversight. Role-based views: Entra RBAC determines what each operator sees — HR BP sees hiring workflows, Finance BP sees budget gates, IT Ops sees provisioning workflows. Each role gets a filtered dashboard with relevant metrics and exception queues. Customisation: operators can configure their view — filter by agency, market, risk level, jurisdiction, client, workflow type. Pin frequently-used filters. Set personal notification preferences. Visual monitoring: real-time workflow status with visual indicators (active, waiting, exception, completed). Fleet health summary from the Fleet Manager. Drill-down from fleet view to individual workflow to specific phase. The Custom Control Plane UI consumes data from Application Insights APIs (traces), Foundry REST APIs (agent inventory), APIM metrics (token/cost), workflow state store (phase status), and Fleet Manager assessments (pushed via SignalR for real-time updates).
Key Technologies: Custom Control Plane UI (React), SignalR (real-time), Entra RBAC, Fleet Manager agent
POC Demo: POC1: Live Control Plane dashboard with Finance Controller view managing 30-50 concurrent invoice workflows. Role-filtered views.

Question: How does the platform prioritise and triage items for human intervention? Describe AI-driven prioritisation by criticality, SLA, and confidence.
Response: The Fleet Manager agent provides AI-driven prioritisation. It consumes telemetry from all workflows and reasons about: (1) Business impact — invoice value, candidate seniority, client priority. (2) SLA urgency — how close is the workflow to breaching its SLA deadline. (3) Confidence score — how confident was the agentic loop in its recommendation (high confidence items may just need rubber-stamp approval, low confidence items need careful review). (4) Pattern detection — is this exception similar to ones the operator has seen before (surface precedents). The Fleet Manager composes a prioritised exception queue: most urgent/impactful items surface first. Low-risk batches are grouped for bulk approval. The operator sees the Fleet Manager's assessment, not raw telemetry. Agent 365 helps determine routing — who should receive each exception based on role, authority, availability, and timezone.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager agent (AI-driven prioritisation), Agent 365 (routing), Custom Control Plane UI
POC Demo: POC2: Show prioritised exception queue — compliance flag on German hire ranked above routine scheduling exception based on risk and SLA.

Question: What contextual information is presented to human reviewers? Describe how history, reasoning, and agent context are surfaced for quick decisions.
Response: Instant situational awareness is a primary design goal — full context within 5 seconds of clicking a workflow. The Control Plane drill-down shows: (1) What happened — timeline of phases completed, actions taken, systems touched. (2) What stopped progress — the specific exception or decision point with full context. (3) What the agent tried — reasoning chain from OTEL traces, tool calls attempted, errors encountered. (4) What the agent recommends — the Fleet Manager's recommendation based on policy, precedents, and data. (5) What the options are — approve as-is, modify and approve, reject, escalate, or override. Supporting context: relevant policy excerpts, similar past decisions, cost impact, SLA status. All powered by the Fleet Manager agent's contextual reasoning over OTEL data and the workflow state store. The human's PA can provide additional coaching and knowledge augmentation on demand.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager agent, OTEL traces, workflow state store, Custom Control Plane UI, PA skill amplification
POC Demo: POC1: Click into an invoice exception — show 5-second situational awareness with full context, recommendation, and options.

Question: How does human feedback loop back into agent improvement? Describe retraining or tuning mechanisms.
Response: Human feedback loops back through three mechanisms. (1) Override logging: when a human overrides an agent recommendation (changes a shortlist, rejects a proposed GL code), the override is logged with full context — the agent's recommendation, the human's decision, and any reason provided. (2) Fleet Manager analysis: the Fleet Manager agent analyses override patterns across workflows. If the same type of override happens repeatedly, it proposes a skill or threshold adjustment — surfaced on the Control Plane for approval before implementation. (3) Skill crystallisation: proven patterns (where human overrides consistently improve outcomes) are codified into deterministic skill updates, reviewed and promoted through the API Center lifecycle. This is not model fine-tuning (we avoid retraining production models). It is operational learning: the system's skills, thresholds, and policies improve based on human expertise, version-controlled and audit-trailed.
Key Technologies: Override logging, Fleet Manager pattern analysis, skill crystallisation via API Center
POC Demo: POC2: Show override logging and Fleet Manager proposing threshold adjustment after repeated similar overrides.

Question: Describe audit logging and compliance reporting: granularity, immutability, and customisable report generation.
Response: Audit logging is comprehensive and immutable. Granularity: every model call, tool call, human interaction, approval decision, policy enforcement event, and state change is logged. OTEL spans capture full execution traces. APIM logs all gateway traffic. GHCP SDK hooks log every tool call with workflow context. The action ledger in the workflow state store records all actions (revocable/non-revocable) with the identity that authorised each. Immutability: Azure Log Analytics with archive tier provides 7-12 year retention (immutability enforced via Azure Storage export with immutability policies). Logs are append-only and tamper-evident. Customisable reporting: Azure Log Analytics supports KQL queries for ad-hoc investigation. Microsoft Sentinel provides security-focused reporting and automated threat detection. The Custom Control Plane UI can generate compliance reports per workflow, per agent, per jurisdiction. Foundry Control Plane provides platform-level compliance dashboards.
Key Technologies: Azure Log Analytics (immutable), OTEL tracing, APIM logging, Microsoft Sentinel, action ledger
POC Demo: POC1: Generate compliance report for a completed invoice workflow — show full audit trail from receipt to payment.
